land.text: the border zone of the Kingdoms of Croatia and Slavonia, where Ferdinand I "began building the defense system" after the Habsburgs were elected kings of Croatia in 1526

region.text: the Croatian-Slavonian border zone, "organized into six Border Fortress Captain Generalcies"

ledger.note: 1553: the Habsburgs establish the Military Frontier against the Ottomans. Infobox "Established: 1553"; ancestors are Sigismund's tabors (1435) and Ferdinand I's defence works after 1526; the Croatian page says "the late 16th century".

region.text: Lika, Kordun, Banovina and the Slavonian sanjaks, the former Ottoman lands that Karlowitz returned

ledger.note: 1699: "The Treaty of Karlowitz returned former Ottoman lands, which were largely absorbed into the frontier." Croatian page: the Frontier covered Lika, Kordun and Banovina. Counterpart set to bosnia-eyalet (the Ottoman province that held the land; Bosnia Eyalet page: lost "the sanjak of Lika" and the Slavonian sanjaks in 1699; Military Frontier page: northern Bosnia 1718-1739) [reviewer eu-18-x, 2026-11-01]. Brodsko-Posavska added: the Bosnia Eyalet page says the eyalet lost "all the Slavonian sanjaks". [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: Slavonian county added]

region.text: lower Slavonia and Syrmia, former Ottoman lands

ledger.note: 26 January 1699 (Karlowitz): the Military Frontier page says it "expanded onto former Ottoman territories in Lika, Kordun, Banija, lower Slavonia, Syrmia" after the Great Turkish War; it gives no date for lower Slavonia and Syrmia within 1699-1702. Vukovar-Srijem and Osijek-Baranja are the researcher's reading of "lower Slavonia" and "Syrmia", and the counterpart is the Ottoman Empire because Syrmia and Osijek were not Bosnian sanjaks. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: added so that the Slavonian counties of the 1699 keyframe have an event]

region.text: the Danube, Tisa, Mureș and Sava sections (1702-1751)

ledger.note: 1702: the river sections are formed on the lands Karlowitz returned: "Danube, Tisa, Mureș, and Sava sections existed (1702 to 1751)". The page names the rivers, not the places. Counterpart set to habsburg-monarchy: the river sections were formed in 1702 on land the Ottomans had ceded at Karlowitz in January 1699 (ottoman-empire dossier, 1699 loss to habsburg-monarchy) [reviewer eu-18-x, 2026-11-01].

region.text: northern Bosnia: "From 1718 to 1739, the frontier included northern Bosnia"

Counterpart set to bosnia-eyalet (the Ottoman province that held the land; Bosnia Eyalet page: lost "the sanjak of Lika" and the Slavonian sanjaks in 1699; Military Frontier page: northern Bosnia 1718-1739) [reviewer eu-18-x, 2026-11-01].

region.text: northern Slavonia, "placed under civil administration as the new Kingdom of Slavonia"

region.text: the Mureș section and the Banat banks of the Tisa and Danube sections, placed under civil administration

The page names rivers, not places, so the Banat bank of the strips is the researcher's reading. [revised after review eu-18-x, 2026-11-01: added]

region.text: the Bačka banks of the Tisa and Danube sections, placed under civil administration

region.text: southern Banat, "out of territories of the Banat of Temeswar"

region.text: Šajkaška, the part of Bačka between the Danube and the Tisa, besides the southern Tisa area that stayed military in 1751

The Tisa row of the section table says a small southern area stayed military in 1751 as part of the Šajkaš Battalion, so only the rest of the circle is a gain in 1763 (the Battalion was "formed in 1763 from parts of the previously abolished Danube and Tisa sections"). wars.name: Austro-Turkish War of 1787-1791
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Sistova (1791) ended the war and the Austrian forces withdrew from Serbia; the Frontier's extent did not change.
wars.note: The pages opened name no other Habsburg-Ottoman war: the Great Turkish War before Karlowitz (1699), the war of 1716-1718 before Passarowitz and the war before 1739 are known here only through the treaties.

certainty.note: A line of fortresses and captaincies against the Ottomans; no survey line on the pages opened.

Regimental districts with dated administrative changes (1745, 1751, 1762, 1851, 1871, 1873, 1881); the Ottoman frontier is the treaty line of Karlowitz and Passarowitz, although the pages give no coordinates. The 1718-1739 northern Bosnian extent and the river sections of 1702-1751 are approximate.

notes: Cliopatria has no row; all 13 keyframes are new and rest on county-level readings of names, because the five pages opened give no map. Gaps: the sixteenth- and seventeenth-century extent; the places of the Danube, Tisa, Mureș and Sava sections (1702-1751); which "eastern parts" of Syrmia went to the Vojvodina in 1848 and when they returned (confidence 1); the Frontier's seat before 1783. Disagreements: Banat Frontier abolished 8 August 1873 (main page), 1871/1872 (Banat page text), 1873 (infobox); Transylvanian frontier ended 1851 (district table, Transylvanian page) or 1853 (infobox); establishment 1553 (infobox) or "late 16th century" (Croatian page). Counterparts needing dossiers: Kingdom of Croatia-Slavonia, Kingdom of Slavonia (1745-1868), Banat of Temeswar (1718-1778), Serbian Vojvodina (1848-1849), the Habsburg Principality of Transylvania (1699-1867). Wikidata id null (wikidata.org unreachable). Type is colony: the Frontier was a military borderland ruled from Vienna (Hofkriegsrat), not a sovereign state. Pages not opened and so not used: Treaty of Karlowitz, Treaty of Passarowitz, Great Turkish War (page budget). Review fix (2026-11-01): (1) The Danube, Tisa and Mureș strips (34 cells) end in 1751, as the section table says ("1702-1751"); the 1751 losses are two events, to banat-of-temeswar for the Banat banks (20 cells) and to habsburg-monarchy for the Bačka banks (10 cells), and the strips are out of the keyframes of 1751-1872. (2) The strips start in 1702, not 1699 (the 1699 keyframe is split). (3) Where I part from the reviewer: the reviewer asked to keep only the Šajkaška circle from 1763; the Tisa row says that "one small area in the south remained under military administration as part of the Šajkaš Battalion" in 1751, so the four cells of the Šajkaška circle on the Tisza strip stay in the shape from 1751 and the 1763 gain is the other six; the Šajkaš Battalion's formation (1763) is dated by the page. (4) The 1873 loss of Šajkaška is a separate event (no month on the page). (5) The 1627 'gain' is removed because no land moved (a change of authority, now in the first keyframe's note). (6) The Slavonian counties (Brodsko-Posavska under the Bosnian counterpart; Vukovar-Srijem and Osijek-Baranja under the Ottoman Empire) have 1699 events. (7) Remaining overlap: the strips of 1718-1750 lie inside the Banat region of banat-of-temeswar (22 cells) because the Banat of Temeswar page gives the whole Banat and the Military Frontier page names the rivers but not their banks; I did not remove them because the 1751 loss would then have nothing to remove. Thin and not done: the 16th- and 17th-century growth (1553-1698 is one shape), the return of eastern Syrmia after the Serbian Vojvodina (confidence 1) and the Austro-Turkish wars of 1716-1718 and 1737-1739 in wars. The Šajkaška circle (20.25 E, 45.2 N, 30 km) is taken minus the Banat region in every keyframe and event, because its east end reached over the Tisza into the Banat of Temeswar (3 cells); Šajkaška is the Bačka part between the Danube and the Tisza.
